## Class III implantable device, MDD certificate under 93/42/EEC

**Class:** III (implantable)
**Route:** Article 120(3a) — notified-body certificate issued under 93/42/EEC
**Deadline:** **31 December 2027**, conditional on Article 120(3c)

| Question | Answer | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Which paragraph applies | 120(3a) — device holds a certificate issued under 93/42/EEC and valid by virtue of 120(2) | `[verified]` |
| Class-dependent date | 31 December 2027 — 120(3a)(a) covers **all class III devices**; "implantable" doesn't change it, since the implantable distinction and the sutures/staples/screws exception list only matter for class IIb | `[verified]` |
| 3c conditions met? | **NOT SUPPLIED** — needs confirmation, see below | `[verified]` |

### The 2027 date is conditional, not automatic

Article 120(3c) is cumulative — **all five** conditions must hold, and two of them had deadlines that have already passed:

- **26 May 2024**: quality management system in place per Article 10(9) — 3c(d)
- **26 May 2024**: formal application lodged with a notified body per Annex VII Section 4.3 — 3c(e)
- **26 September 2024**: written agreement signed between you and the notified body — 3c(e)
- Ongoing: continued compliance with 93/42/EEC; **no significant changes** to design or intended purpose; no unacceptable risk to health or safety

If any of those 2024 dates was missed, the extension was never available to this device and the answer is not 31 December 2027. Since today is 17 September 2026, those are settled historical facts rather than things you can still fix — so please confirm them.

Note also **120(3d)**: even while you're running on the MDD certificate, MDR's requirements for post-market surveillance, market surveillance, vigilance, and registration of economic operators and devices apply **in place of** the corresponding 93/42/EEC requirements. That obligation is live now, not in 2027.

### What would change this

Whether the 3c conditions were met — specifically the QMS by 26 May 2024, the application by 26 May 2024, and the signed agreement by 26 September 2024. Also whether any design or intended-purpose change since has crossed the "significant change" line under 3c(b), which would end the derogation regardless of the date.

One thing worth flagging: **26 May 2024 is no longer the market deadline** (that was the original 2017 text, superseded by Regulation (EU) 2023/607), but it hasn't become irrelevant either — it's the date the 2027 extension hangs on.

## Limits

> This covers MDR Article 120(3) and (3a)–(3d) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607, retrieved verbatim from the Official Journal on 2026-09-10. It does **not** cover Article 120's other paragraphs, **IVDR Article 110** (the parallel IVD transition, whose dates differ), MDCG guidance including on what counts as a significant change, Annex VII, or national practice. The transition is conditional and fact-specific; this is a first-pass aid, not legal or regulatory advice, and not a substitute for your notified body or a qualified regulatory professional.

Two things this skill can't answer for you: the rules on how long your MDD certificate itself stays valid live in Article 120(2), and the treatment of units already placed on the market before the deadline lives in later paragraphs — neither is in the reference text I have. If you paste those provisions I'll work from them, but I won't give you dates I can't cite.

## Short answer

**31 December 2027** — for a Class III implantable device covered by a valid MDD certificate under the extended transition (Article 120(3a) MDR, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607). That's roughly 15 months from today.

From 1 January 2028 you cannot *place* new units on the EU market without an MDR certificate. Units lawfully placed on the market before that date can continue to be made available and put into service indefinitely — the old 27 May 2025 "sell-off" deadline was deleted by 2023/607.

## The catch: the conditions were gates in the past, not the future

The 31 December 2027 date only applies if *all* of these were true. For Class III devices the first two are hard deadlines that have already passed:

| Condition | Deadline |
|---|---|
| MDR-compliant QMS in place (Art. 10(9)) | **26 May 2024** |
| Formal MDR conformity assessment application lodged with a notified body | **26 May 2024** |
| Written agreement signed with that notified body | **26 September 2024** |
| Device still complies with MDD | ongoing |
| No significant change in design or intended purpose | ongoing |
| No unacceptable risk to health and safety | ongoing |

If you missed the May/September 2024 gates, you do not have until 2027 — you lost the extension and have been placing a non-compliant device on the market since 26 May 2024. The only routes then are a national derogation under Art. 59(1) or Art. 97(1) MDR, or stopping. **Verify the application date and the signed NB agreement before relying on the 2027 date** — that's the first thing I'd check.

Two other things that change the answer:
- **Custom-made Class III implantables** had a separate, earlier deadline: **26 May 2026**, which has already passed.
- If your MDD certificate had a nominal expiry that lapsed before 20 March 2023, it's only deemed valid if you'd signed the NB agreement before expiry or hold a competent-authority derogation.

## While you're in the transition

MDD certification doesn't mean MDD rules across the board. MDR requirements already apply in place of the MDD equivalents for post-market surveillance, vigilance, market surveillance, and registration of economic operators and devices. Also worth confirming your current status on:

- **Eudamed** — actor, device/UDI and certificate module registration became mandatory in phases under Regulation (EU) 2024/1860.
- **Supply interruption notice** — Art. 10a MDR requires ~6 months' advance notification to competent authorities and health institutions if you intend to discontinue. Relevant if the realistic plan is to exit rather than certify.

## Practical read on the timeline

15 months is tight but not unusual for a Class III implantable review that's already in progress. Notified body queues are the binding constraint, not the regulation. If the technical documentation review hasn't produced a first round of deficiency questions yet, that's the schedule risk to escalate now — there is no further extension mechanism beyond Art. 59/97 derogations, which are granted case-by-case and typically only on shortage/public-health grounds.

One caveat: my reliable knowledge runs to May 2026, and the Commission has had a broader MDR/IVDR revision in the works. Confirm against the current consolidated text of Article 120 and MDCG guidance that no further amendment has shifted these dates. This is a regulatory summary, not legal advice — your RA lead or notified body should confirm the specifics for this certificate.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
**31 December 2027** — provided you met the 2024 milestones. Otherwise the answer is "you already can't."

## The rule

Article 120 MDR as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607 extends legacy MDD certificate validity on a risk-class staircase. Class III implantables sit in the earliest bucket:

- **31 Dec 2027** — Class III and Class IIb implantables (excluding the listed "well-established technology" items: sutures, staples, dental fillings, braces, crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips, connectors)
- **31 Dec 2028** — everything else (other IIb, IIa, Is/Im), plus Class III custom-made implantables

This holds **even if the certificate's own printed expiry date is earlier** — the extension operates by law, not by the notified body reissuing anything.

## The conditions (Art. 120(3c)) — check these now

The extension is conditional, and two conditions had hard dates that are behind us:

1. Device continues to comply with the MDD
2. No significant change in design or intended purpose
3. No unacceptable risk to health and safety
4. **By 26 May 2024** — MDR-compliant QMS in place (Art. 10(9))
5. **By 26 May 2024** — formal MDR conformity assessment application lodged with a notified body, **and by 26 Sep 2024** — signed written agreement with that notified body

If 4 and 5 weren't met, the extension never attached to your device and its lawful placing on the market ended when the original certificate lapsed. That's the first thing to verify before planning around 2027.

## Two things people get wrong

**Sell-off.** The old 26 May 2025 sell-off deadline in Art. 120(4) was **deleted** by 2023/607. Units lawfully *placed on the market* before 31 Dec 2027 can continue to be made available and put into service with no end date. So the cliff is on placing on the market — distributor and hospital stock isn't stranded.

**MDR already applies in part.** During the transition, MDR requirements for post-market surveillance, market surveillance, vigilance, and registration of economic operators and devices apply *in place of* the MDD equivalents. Your legacy device is not fully outside MDR today. Also note the Art. 10a supply-interruption notification duty (from Reg. 2024/1860), in effect since 10 Jan 2025.

Your MDD notified body remains responsible for surveillance of the legacy certificate until your MDR notified body takes over under a written transfer arrangement.

## Practical read

Notified body capacity is the binding constraint, not the legal date. A Class III implantable review realistically needs 12–18 months from complete technical documentation, and incomplete submissions are where schedules die. Working back from 31 Dec 2027, you want the certificate decision — not the submission — as the thing you're tracking.

Watch for the Commission's targeted MDR revision proposal, signalled for late 2026. Nothing has moved the 2027 date, and I wouldn't plan on it doing so.

Worth confirming with your notified body in writing that they consider the Art. 120(3c) conditions satisfied for this device — that's the documentation you'll want if a competent authority asks why you're still shipping.

graders.evidence:
**31 December 2027** — that's the hard stop for *placing on the market* a Class III implantable legacy device, and only if your company hit a set of milestones that fell in 2024. Worth verifying those first, because if any was missed the certificate's extension never attached and the device is already off-market as of now.

## The rule

MDD/AIMDD certificates don't get extended by their own terms — Article 120(3a)–(3c) MDR, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607, deems them valid beyond their printed expiry date. For Class III devices and Class IIb implantables (other than the "well-established technology" list — sutures, staples, dental fillings, crowns, screws, plates, wires, pins, clips, connectors), that deemed validity runs to **31 December 2027**. Everything else in the legacy pool runs to 31 December 2028.

## Conditions — all of these, and two are already in the past

1. The certificate was valid on 26 May 2021 and hadn't been withdrawn.
2. The device still complies with the MDD, and there have been **no significant changes** in design or intended purpose since. This is device-by-device: one significant change voids the extension for that device only.
3. The device presents no unacceptable risk to health and safety.
4. By **26 May 2024**, an MDR Article 10(9) quality management system was in place.
5. By **26 May 2024**, a formal MDR conformity-assessment application was lodged with a notified body, **and** by **26 September 2024** a written agreement was signed with that notified body.

Since both of those last dates have passed, the practical question for you is documentary: pull the application acknowledgement and the signed NB agreement and confirm the device in question is inside the scope of both. Also confirm your MDR notified body has taken over surveillance of the legacy device — that transfers on signature of the written agreement.

## The part people usually miss

31 December 2027 caps **placing on the market** (first making available in the EU — typically your shipment to a distributor or customer). Regulation (EU) 2023/607 **deleted the sell-off deadline** from Article 120(4). So units you have lawfully placed on the market by that date can continue to be made available down the chain and put into service with no time limit. Practically, that means stocking distributor inventory ahead of the date buys you runway on the *supply* side — it does not buy you any more time to manufacture and ship new units.

## If a milestone was missed

You're not covered by the transition and the route back is either completing MDR certification, or a national derogation under Article 59 MDR from the competent authority where the device is needed (granted in the interest of public health / patient safety, usually narrow and time-limited). Don't plan around that as a commercial strategy.

## Watch item

The Commission has signalled a broader targeted revision of the MDR/IVDR framework. Nothing adopted changes the 2027 date, so plan against 31 December 2027 and treat any further relief as upside, not schedule.

One caveat: this is a read of the regulation, not legal advice — confirm the milestone evidence and scope with your notified body and regulatory counsel before you rely on the date.
